facts.statement: Garrigatitan is a genus of titanosaurian dinosaur that lived during the late Cretaceous Period in France.
facts.quote: Garrigatitan (meaning "garrigue giant") is a genus of titanosaurian dinosaur from the late Cretaceous Period of the Grès à Reptiles Formation in France.

facts.statement: The genus Garrigatitan contains only one known species, Garrigatitan meridionalis.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, Garrigatitan meridionalis.

facts.statement: Excavations to find Garrigatitan fossils took place at Velaux-La Bastide Neuve between 2009 and 2012.
facts.quote: Between 2009 and 2012, excavations were carried out at Velaux-La Bastide Neuve by the Palaios Association and the University of Poitiers.

facts.statement: Garrigatitan meridionalis was named and described in 2021 by a team led by Verónica Díez Díaz.
facts.quote: In 2021, the type species Garrigatitan meridionalis was named and described by Verónica Díez Díaz, Géraldine Garcia, Xabier Pereda Suberbiola, Benjamin Jentgen-Ceschino, Koen Stein, Pascal Godefroit and Xavier Valentin.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Garrigatitan dates to the late Campanian stage of the Cretaceous.
facts.quote: The holotype, MMS / VBN.09.17, was found in a layer of sandstone of the Begudian, the second level of the second series, dating back to the late Campanian.

facts.statement: The holotype fossil is a sacrum belonging to an immature individual of Garrigatitan.
facts.quote: It consists of a sacrum belonging to an immature individual.

facts.statement: The name Garrigatitan combines the Occitan word for a dry thicket and the Greek word for a giant.
facts.quote: The generic name, Garrigatitan, is a combination of the Occitan "garriga," meaning "dry thicket", referring to a type of Mediterranean vegetation characterized by drought-resistant shrubs, and the Greek "titan", after the Greek mythological family of giants.

facts.statement: Some Garrigatitan specimens are estimated to have been 4 to 6 meters long and weighed 2 to 2.5 metric tons.
facts.quote: Some Garrigatitan specimens are regarded as subadults or adults belonged to individuals measuring 4 - 6 m long and weighing 2 - 2.5 MT.

facts.statement: A tentatively referred adult specimen of Garrigatitan is estimated to have been 12 to 16 meters long.
facts.quote: A tentatively referred specimen belonged to an adult individual measuring about 12 - 16 m long.

facts.statement: Initial phylogenetic analysis placed Garrigatitan within the titanosaur subfamily Lirainosaurinae.
facts.quote: In their phylogenetic analysis, Díez Díaz et al. recovered Garrigatitan as a membr of the titanosaur subfamily Lirainosaurinae.

facts.statement: A 2024 analysis recovered Garrigatitan as a non-lirainosaurine titanosaur within the clade Lognkosauria, related to genera like Notocolossus and Patagotitan.
facts.quote: In their 2024 description of Qunkasaura, Mocho et al. included Garrigatitan in their phylogenetic analysis, recovering it as a late-diverging non-lirainosaurine within the Lognkosauria, closely related to the South American genera Notocolossus, Patagotitan, and Puertasaurus.

facts.statement: Garrigatitan is classified within the family Saltasauridae.
Garrigatitan lived approximately 74 to 70 million years ago during the Campanian stage of the late Cretaceous in what is now Europe.

facts.statement: The time range for Garrigatitan is estimated from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)
